newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says has sufficient rice stocks.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says has sufficient rice stocks.

text.p: Indonesia said on Tuesday it had sufficient rice stocks and did not expect to import the staple despite a drought plaguing the archipelago.

"Our rice stocks are currently 3.0 million tonnes. It is sufficient despite the drought. We don't need to import," Beddu Amang, chairman of commodities regulator BULOG, told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
He said Suharto had ordered BULOG to stabilise commodity prices, including those of rice, amid a sharp fall in the rupiah against the U.S. dollar in recent weeks.

"We must keep prices stable. The dollar's movement should not influence commodity prices, especially those produced domestically," he said, adding that BULOG would intervene in the markets when necessary.
"BULOG's function is to stabilise prices," he added.
Amang said prices of commodities such as sugar, wheat flour and soybeans were generally stable.

Indonesia was still importing around 600,000 tonnes of soybean a year, he said, adding that Indonesia's crude palm oil production was projected to rise to 5.2-5.3 million tonnes in 1997, compared with 4.5 million tonnes last year.
He said the price of palm olein had increased to 1,640 rupiah/kg from 1,380 rupiah in July. Amang said, however, that the "appropriate" price was 1,600 rupiah/kg.
"The (price) increase was due to a reduction in supply to the local market because of increased exports," he said.
He said exports have been increasing following a reduction in export taxes on crude palm oil and its products under the government's July economic deregulation package.
Amang also said state plantations would increase their monthly crude palm oil allocations to BULOG to 20,000 tonnes from 10,000 tonnes previously.
"The deregulation package encourages exports. Our duty to stabilise local prices has been made difficult, therefore we have asked state plantations for additional supply," he said.
BULOG intervenes in the palm oil market when it considers prices are not reasonable.
